items.title: Foundation & delivery
items.goal: A developer can clone the repo, run the app locally against a local Supabase stack, and every pull request gets checked by CI and deployed to a Vercel preview in `sin1`. Errors reach Sentry without carrying personal data.
prd: Technical architecture → Next.js App Router in TypeScript, Supabase backend, Vercel sin1, Supabase ap-southeast-1 → decided
Technical architecture → UI components (Tailwind + shadcn/ui), AI access (Vercel AI SDK), monitoring (Sentry), testing (Vitest, Playwright, eval) → proposed
Environments & delivery (suggested) → one repo, preview per PR, 2 Supabase projects, CI applies migrations → suggested
Security (suggested) → secret key only in Vercel env; rate-limit AI routes; monthly spend cap → suggested
Free-tier limits → Vercel Hobby non-commercial; one region; cron once a day → decided (which paid plan: open)
exit: `npm run dev`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `test`, `build` all work from a clean clone
CI runs lint, typecheck, unit tests and build on every PR, and Playwright against the preview
A pull request produces a working Vercel preview with functions in `sin1`
Sentry receives a test error from server and client with no candidate data in the event
outOfScope: Any screen or feature UI (P2 onward)
Sign-in of any kind — the MVP has none
Paid plans and backups — PRD open questions for the real-data release

items.title: Developers can run the app locally and it deploys to Vercel sin1
items.story: As a developer, I want a scaffolded Next.js app with typed env handling, tests and error reporting, so that every later task starts from a working, checked baseline instead of re-deciding the basics.
ac: Given a clean clone and `npm install`, when I run `npm run dev`, then the app serves a page locally with no runtime error.
Given a missing or malformed environment variable, when the app starts, then it fails with a message naming the variable, and no secret value is printed.
Given `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` and `npm run build`, when each is run, then all four pass on the scaffold.
Given an unhandled error on the server or in the browser, when it is thrown, then Sentry receives it and the event contains no candidate name, email, phone or CV text.
prd: Technical architecture → Frontend: Next.js (App Router) in TypeScript → decided
Technical architecture → UI components: Tailwind + shadcn/ui → proposed
Technical architecture → Monitoring: Vercel runtime logs plus Sentry → proposed
Technical architecture → Testing: Vitest, Playwright, AI quality script → proposed

items.title: Scaffold the Next.js App Router app with TypeScript strict, Tailwind and shadcn/ui
items.what: Create the Next.js App Router application with TypeScript in strict mode, Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui initialised, the folder layout from `nextjs-app`, and the npm scripts named in CLAUDE.md. Pin Vercel functions to `sin1`.
scope: `create-next-app` with App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, ESLint and the `src/` directory
`tsconfig.json` with `strict: true`
`npx shadcn@latest init` with the default theme; real tokens arrive in E02-S01-T02
Folder layout per `nextjs-app`: `src/app`, `src/components`, `src/lib`, `src/server` with `import "server-only"`
npm scripts `dev`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `build` exactly as named in CLAUDE.md
`vercel.json` (or the equivalent route config) pinning functions to `sin1`
A placeholder home page — no product UI
exclusions: Any product screen, component or route beyond a placeholder
done: `npm run dev`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` all pass from a clean clone
`tsconfig.json` has `strict: true` and the build has no `any` outside commented exceptions
Functions are pinned to `sin1` in committed configuration
`src/server` exists and its index is marked `import "server-only"`

items.title: Add the typed env schema with a server-only / public split
items.what: Parse and validate every environment variable once, at startup, with Zod. Server secrets must be unreachable from client code, and `.env.example` must list every variable by name with no values. Test-first: the parser's failure behaviour is logic.
scope: `src/lib/env.ts` (public) and `src/server/env.ts` (server-only) with Zod schemas
Failing tests first: a missing required variable throws naming the variable; a malformed URL is rejected; no secret value appears in the thrown message
`.env.example` listing every variable name from the infrastructure plan, values blank
A lint or build-time guard that a `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` name is never used for a secret
exclusions: Creating the Vercel project or its environments (E01-S04-T01)
done: Failing tests exist first and then pass: missing variable, malformed value, and no secret in the error message
`.env.example` contains every variable name and no value
Importing the server env module from a client component fails the build or the lint rule

items.title: Set up Vitest and Playwright with desktop and phone projects
items.what: Add the test tooling the strategy record specifies: Vitest for unit tests with no network, and Playwright with `desktop` (1440×900) and `phone` (390×844, `isMobile`) projects. One smoke test each, plus the `test`, `test:e2e` and `test:db` scripts.
scope: Vitest config and setup: fake timers available, unexpected `fetch` fails the test, fictional fixtures folder `test/fixtures/`
Playwright config with the two projects and a web server pointing at the dev server
One passing unit smoke test and one passing e2e smoke test per project
npm scripts `test`, `test:e2e` and `test:db` exactly as named in CLAUDE.md (`test:db` may be a stub that explains it needs Docker until E03 lands)
exclusions: Any product test — those belong to their feature tasks
done: `npm test` passes and makes no network call
`npm run test:e2e` passes for both the `desktop` and `phone` projects
The phone smoke test asserts `document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= window.innerWidth`
An accidental `fetch` in a unit test fails that test

items.title: Add Sentry for server and client errors with no personal data in events
items.what: Wire Sentry for server and browser errors, and scrub events so no candidate data, CV text, AI prompt content or secret can leave the app. The PRD lists monitoring as proposed; this implements it as written.
scope: Sentry initialisation for server and client, DSN read through the typed env module
A `beforeSend` scrubber that strips request bodies, known personal-data field names and any value matching a secret-shaped pattern
Tests for the scrubber: a candidate name, an email, CV text and a key-shaped string are all removed
A documented way to send a test error from each runtime
exclusions: Alerting rules or notification channels — the portal sends no email and alerts live on the dashboard
done: A deliberate server error and a deliberate client error both reach Sentry in a preview deployment
Failing-then-passing unit tests prove the scrubber removes name, email, CV text and secret-shaped values
No DSN or token is committed; the DSN comes from the env module

items.title: Supabase dev and prod projects are wired to the app
items.story: As a developer, I want a local Supabase stack, a migrations folder and a server-only database client, so that schema work in the next phase has somewhere to go and the browser can never reach the database.
ac: Given Docker is running, when I run the Supabase CLI start command, then a local stack comes up and generated database types are written into the repo.
Given any client component, when it tries to import the Supabase client, then the build fails.
Given the publishable key, when it is used against any table, then it reads nothing, because RLS is on with no public policies.
prd: Technical architecture → Backend: Supabase Postgres, Storage, Edge Functions if needed → decided
Technical architecture → Database region: ap-southeast-1 → decided
Security (suggested) → secret key only in Vercel env; RLS on with no public policies → suggested
Environments & delivery → Supabase Free allows 2 active projects: dev/preview and prod → suggested

items.title: Initialise the Supabase CLI, migrations folder and generated types
items.what: Set up Supabase locally: `supabase init`, the migrations folder, a local stack a developer can start with Docker, and a script that regenerates TypeScript types from the schema into the repo.
scope: `supabase/config.toml` and the `supabase/migrations/` folder
A type-generation script writing `src/lib/database.types.ts`
`npm run test:db` wired to a Vitest config that runs against the local stack
A README section: how to start the stack, apply migrations and regenerate types
exclusions: Any table, policy or view — that is E03
Linking to a remote Supabase project or applying anything remotely
done: The local stack starts and `supabase migration list` runs clean on an empty migrations folder
Type generation produces a committed `database.types.ts` that typechecks
`npm run test:db` runs and reports zero tests rather than failing

items.title: Add the server-only Supabase client using the secret key
items.what: Create the single Supabase client the app uses, in server code only, holding the secret key that bypasses RLS. Prove with tests that the key cannot reach the browser bundle. Test-first.
scope: `src/server/db.ts` marked `import "server-only"`, typed from `database.types.ts`
Failing tests first: importing from a client module fails; the built client bundle contains no secret; the client is a singleton per request as `nextjs-app` requires
A build-time check that greps the client bundle for the secret-key variable name
exclusions: A browser Supabase client — the app never has one
done: Failing-then-passing tests prove a client component cannot import the server client
A check over the production bundle finds no Supabase secret and is wired into `npm run build` or CI
The client is typed against the generated database types

items.title: Every pull request runs the CI checks
items.story: As a reviewer, I want lint, typecheck, unit tests, build, migrations and end-to-end tests to run automatically on every pull request, so that a review is about the design rather than about whether it works.
ac: Given a pull request, when CI runs, then lint, typecheck, unit tests and build all report status on the PR.
Given a pull request that changes a migration, when CI runs, then the migrations are applied to an ephemeral local Supabase and the DB integration tests run.
Given a Vercel preview is ready, when the Playwright job runs, then it tests the preview URL at both desktop and phone width.
Given a workflow needs a secret, when it runs on a fork or without that secret, then the job is skipped with a clear message rather than failing.
prd: Environments & delivery (suggested) → CI applies migrations with the Supabase CLI and runs the tests and AI quality script → suggested
Non-functional requirements → Testing: Vitest, Playwright, AI quality script → proposed

items.title: Add the PR checks workflow: lint, typecheck, unit tests, build
items.what: Add the GitHub Actions workflow that gates every pull request on lint, typecheck, unit tests and build, with npm caching, least-privilege permissions and a concurrency group that cancels superseded runs.
scope: `.github/workflows/pr-checks.yml` on `pull_request` and on `push` to `main`
Node version pinned, `npm ci`, npm cache
`permissions: contents: read` and nothing more
Concurrency group keyed on the ref, cancelling in-progress runs
A job summary listing which checks ran
exclusions: End-to-end, migration and eval jobs (T02, T03, E11-S03-T02)
Deployment — Vercel handles that from its own integration
done: The workflow runs green on a pull request that touches app code
It uses least-privilege permissions and cancels superseded runs
It needs no repository secret

items.title: Add the Playwright CI job against the Vercel preview
items.what: Run the end-to-end suite in CI against the pull request's Vercel preview deployment at both desktop and phone width, waiting for the deployment to be ready and skipping cleanly when no preview exists.
scope: `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` triggered on `deployment_status` (or waiting on the Vercel check) so it runs when the preview is ready
Both Playwright projects run; the base URL comes from the deployment
Traces and the HTML report uploaded as artifacts on failure only
Skip with a clear message when the preview URL is unavailable
exclusions: Writing product e2e tests — feature tasks own those
done: The job runs both projects against a real preview URL and reports on the PR
On failure it uploads the Playwright report as an artifact
With no preview available, the job skips rather than fails

items.title: Validate migrations and run DB integration tests in CI
items.what: On any change under `supabase/`, start an ephemeral local Supabase in CI, apply every migration from scratch, run the DB integration tests, and fail if a migration is not reversible or not idempotent as the project requires.
scope: .github/workflows/db.yml with a path filter on `supabase/**`
Supabase CLI in CI: start, apply all migrations to an empty database, run `npm run test:db`
A check that the migration set applies cleanly twice in a row where the project requires idempotency
Job summary reporting the migrations applied
exclusions: Applying migrations to any remote project — that belongs to the release workflow (E12-S01-T01)
done: A pull request touching `supabase/**` triggers the job and it passes on a clean database
The DB integration tests run against the ephemeral stack
A deliberately broken migration fails the job

items.title: Previews and production deploy safely and cannot run up costs
items.story: As the agency director, I want every pull request to get a preview and the AI routes to be rate-limited with a spend cap, so that an open portal with no sign-in cannot cost us money or break Vercel's terms without us noticing.
ac: Given a pull request, when Vercel builds it, then a preview deployment is available with functions in `sin1` and preview environment variables.
Given the AI routes, when they are called rapidly from one source, then the Vercel firewall rate limit rejects the excess.
Given Vercel Hobby forbids commercial use, when recruiters are about to use the portal for real work, then the plan decision is recorded as open with an owner rather than assumed.
prd: Environments & delivery → every PR gets a Vercel preview; main deploys to production → suggested
Security (suggested) → a Vercel firewall rule rate-limits the AI routes and the provider has a monthly spend cap → suggested
Free-tier limits → Vercel Hobby is non-commercial only → decided; which paid plan → open

items.title: Configure the Vercel project, regions and per-environment variables
items.what: Connect the repository to the Vercel project `u-recruitment`, pin functions to `sin1`, set the environment variables for development, preview and production from the infrastructure plan, and record the Hobby non-commercial question as open.
scope: Vercel project settings: region `sin1`, preview per pull request, production from `main`
Environment variables set per environment through the Vercel dashboard or CLI — **names from `.env.example`, values never committed**
A written note in `docs/plans/infrastructure.md` recording which variables are set where
Recording the Hobby non-commercial limit as an open decision with an owner, linked from the open-questions register
exclusions: Choosing or buying a paid plan — that is a PRD open question
Creating Supabase projects with real data
done: A pull request produces a working preview deployment with functions reported in `sin1`
Every variable in `.env.example` is present in the right Vercel environments, with no value in the repository
The open-questions register links this as the Vercel plan decision, still open
verify: grep -RIn 'vercel.com' docs/ | head   # no tokens or secrets

items.title: Rate-limit the AI routes and document the monthly spend cap
items.what: Put a Vercel firewall rate limit in front of every AI route and record how the provider's monthly spend cap is set, because without sign-in anyone with the link could otherwise run up AI costs. Configuration is committed; the in-app spend check lands in E11-S04-T01.
scope: Vercel firewall rule or committed configuration limiting requests to the AI route paths
A single documented path prefix for AI routes so the rule has one thing to match
`docs/plans/infrastructure.md`: how the provider spend cap is set and who checks it
A note on what happens to a rate-limited request in the UI: a clear message, never a silent failure
exclusions: The in-app monthly spend cap check (E11-S04-T01)
Choosing the provider or setting a real budget figure
done: Every AI route sits under one documented path prefix and the rate limit matches it
The rate-limited response is documented and produces a clear user-facing message
The spend-cap procedure is written down with an owner
